The heaviest chain of tasks, the critical path B, D, F, G, is drawn in the accent color: its durations 3 + 4 + 2 add up to 9.0, more than any other route from a source to G." width="100%"} In a DAG of tasks and dependencies, the longest path is the *critical path*: the chain of tasks that determines the earliest possible finish time, so that any delay along it delays the whole project. On an unweighted graph its length is the number of edges; on a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) it is the total edge weight, so weights can carry task durations. Edges without a weight count as `1.0`, and of several parallel edges the heaviest counts. Unlike shortest paths, longest paths are only well defined without cycles, so the graph must be a DAG. The length is available from `dag_longest_path_length()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node IDs along a longest path, in order. When several paths tie, the one ending at (and then extending from) the lowest node ID is returned. An empty graph gives an empty list; a graph without edges gives a single node. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or contains a cycle. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~dag_longest_path_length`) : The length of the longest path. [](`~topological_generations`) : Group the nodes into layers. [](`~shortest_path`) : The shortest path between two nodes. ## Examples {.doc-examples} With task durations as weights, the longest path runs through the slow test suite, though the documentation branch starts with the longer first task: ::: {#1df1d46b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("fetch", "compile", 3.0), ("compile", "test", 10.0), ("test", "package", 2.0), ("fetch", "docs", 4.0), ("docs", "publish", 1.0)], directed=True, ) [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in graph.dag_longest_path()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['fetch', 'compile', 'test', 'package'] ``` ::: ::: ### The critical path `project()` is the plan for opening a made-up café, with an arrow from each task to every task that can't start until it's done, weighted by the days the first task takes. The longest path is the critical path, the chain of tasks that sets how soon the café can open: from signing the lease through the design, permits, build-out, installation and training. Here each task is sized by the days it takes: ::: {#9d60e11d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} cafe = ec.project() critical = cafe.dag_longest_path() [cafe.get_label_from_id(n) for n in critical] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['Start', 'Sign lease', 'Design', 'Permits', 'Build out', 'Install', 'Training', 'Soft opening', 'Finish'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#a4539e6c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} cafe.plot( layout="pos", highlight=critical, size_by="days", label_by="label", height=360, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### The longest chain of prerequisites `courses()` is unweighted, so its longest path is the one with the most courses, the math sequence leading to CS460: ::: {#338c346f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} courses = ec.courses() chain = courses.dag_longest_path() [courses.get_label_from_id(n) for n in chain] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['MATH101', 'MATH102', 'MATH210', 'STAT201', 'CS360', 'CS460'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#e259a4b7 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} stages = dict(enumerate(courses.topological_generations())) courses.layout_multipartite(subset_key=stages).plot( layout="pos", highlight=chain, label_by="label", height=420, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: [Directed acyclic graphs](../user-guide/dags.qmd#the-critical-path) finds the critical path of building a house, and the slack of every task.
